title: China, Kimi K3 and WAICO: Can Beijing win the AI race and make the rules too?
gist: China is pairing frontier open-weight models (Moonshot AI's 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3, Alibaba's Qwen at nearly a billion downloads) with a new Shanghai-based standards body, WAICO, whose 29 founding members are all Global South states, to convert cheap distributable model access into rule-setting power. The article argues the US and China are running different races — closed proprietary models tied to AGI security and military use versus cheap open weights plus institution-building — and flags two Chinese vulnerabilities: possible curbs on exporting model weights and 320 million gig workers exposed to AI job displacement.

insights.claim: China's bid to set global AI rules is only credible because its frontier models have won broad international adoption; without competitive models, Beijing's governance overtures would carry no weight.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Model leaderboard position is now a geopolitical variable — watch Chinese benchmark standing as a leading indicator of standards-body influence.
insights.quote: But without the impressive AI models that have gained a broad following around the world, Beijing’s overtures to lead AI governance would lack traction.
insights.locator: But without the impressive AI models

insights.claim: Moonshot AI timed the launch of Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight LLM, to land just before China opened the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization conference in Shanghai in July 2026.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Chinese frontier releases are being sequenced around diplomatic events — expect model launches clustered ahead of the next WAICO summit.
insights.quote: Just before the conference opened, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 – a powerful Large Language Model (LLM) with 2.8 trillion parameters – was launched.
insights.locator: Just before the conference opened

insights.claim: Kimi K3 ranks in the top three of the Vals Index behind only two Claude models, putting a Chinese lab within one tier of the US frontier rather than a generation behind.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: The capability gap argument for US export-control-based containment weakens if a top-three model is downloadable for free.
insights.quote: Kimi K3 is currently ranked in the top three on the Vals Index after two Claude LLMs, taking the Chinese model to the forefront of global AI tech.
insights.locator: Kimi K3 is currently ranked in the top three

insights.claim: China's AI ambition is a decade-old state plan, not an opportunistic response: the 2017 Next Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan set a target of becoming the world's primary AI innovation centre by 2030.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
entities: Next Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan
insights.so_what: Policy continuity means Chinese AI subsidy and diffusion strategy is unlikely to reverse on cyclical pressure; underwrite it as a structural trend to 2030.
insights.locator: Back in 2017, its Next Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan

themes.theme: Open weights vs closed weights as competing business models

insights.claim: The central US–China AI divide is distribution model, not raw capability: China popularizes computationally efficient open-weight models that are free or cheap to download, while US labs rely on closed proprietary models users cannot download or modify.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Comparing the two countries on benchmark scores alone misreads the contest — the relevant scoreboard is installed base and derivative models.
insights.quote: In several key respects, the two superpowers are running very different races.
insights.locator: In several key respects, the two superpowers

insights.claim: Chinese models compete on cost per million output tokens as much as on quality, offering cutting-edge performance at prices materially below leading US models.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Sustained price undercutting at the frontier compresses inference margins for closed US labs and pressures per-token pricing globally.
insights.quote: The Chinese model provides cutting-edge performance with an open-weight format – and can be operated much more cheaply (per million output tokens) than the leading US models.
insights.locator: The Chinese model provides cutting-edge performance

insights.claim: Alibaba's Qwen family has accumulated nearly one billion cumulative downloads, evidence that China's open-weight strategy is producing real global installed base rather than just headlines.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Download share is becoming the metric that determines whose defaults, tooling and safety conventions the world's developers inherit.
insights.quote: the suite of Qwen models from Alibaba have racked up nearly one billion cumulative downloads
insights.locator: And it is proving to be a very successful strategy

insights.claim: The US closed-weight posture is driven by two non-commercial motives — keeping security high while OpenAI and Anthropic pursue AGI, and the technology's importance to the US military — so it will not shift on competitive logic alone.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect US openness to be decided in national-security channels, not by product teams — policy risk sits upstream of company strategy.
insights.locator: One reason for this approach is to maintain a high level of security

themes.theme: WAICO and the Global South coalition

insights.claim: All 29 founding members of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization are Global South countries — including Indonesia, Brazil, Malaysia, South Africa, Senegal, Russia and Pakistan — making WAICO a deliberately non-Western standards bloc from inception.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A parallel standards body with numerical majority potential can fragment AI compliance regimes for any multinational deploying models globally.
insights.quote: all 29 founding members of WAICO are countries of the Global South, including Indonesia, Brazil, Malaysia, South Africa, Senegal, Russia and Pakistan
insights.locator: Indeed, all 29 founding members of WAICO

insights.claim: Beijing intends to expand WAICO membership substantially and mostly from the Global South, according to a private conversation with a Chinese official — the aim is to use those countries' agency to set international AI norms.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Track WAICO accession announcements as the concrete measure of whether Chinese norm-setting is gaining or stalling.
insights.quote: Beijing has plans to vastly expand WAICO’s membership, mostly through further additions from the Global South, according to a private conversation with a Chinese official.
insights.locator: Beijing has plans to vastly expand WAICO’s membership

insights.claim: China is backing its AI diplomacy with roughly 5,000 training opportunities routed through cooperation centres in ASEAN, the African Union, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS — forums it leads or is a key member of.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Capacity-building creates practitioner lock-in to Chinese stacks in emerging markets long before procurement decisions are formally made.
insights.locator: China has outlined plans to provide some 5,000 training opportunities

insights.claim: Xi Jinping framed WAICO in the language of redistributive justice — pledging to help Global South countries bridge AI and digital divides and to prevent creating new historical injustice in AI — building on China's Global AI Governance Action Plan.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: The rhetorical frame is designed to make Western export controls read as exclusion, raising the diplomatic cost of US containment policy.
insights.quote: ‘help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides’ and ‘prevent creating new historical injustice in AI’
insights.locator: In his speech to announce WAICO

insights.claim: China's governance vision explicitly rejects an AGI path in which models train themselves autonomously into a superintelligent system beyond human control, positioning Beijing as the anti-autonomy pole of global AI policy.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Chinese and Western AI-safety vocabularies now overlap, which makes joint declarations easier to sign and harder to interpret.
insights.locator: Another feature of China’s vision for global AI governance

insights.claim: In the Chinese framing, 'human control' of AI operationally means control by Communist party bodies such as the Cyberspace Administration of China — a substantive difference hidden inside shared safety language.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Any WAICO-drafted 'human oversight' standard could import state-control requirements into rules that Western firms would have to meet abroad.
insights.quote: Human control in China’s context effectively means under the control of key Communist party bodies such as the Cyberspace Administration of China.
insights.locator: Human control in China’s context

insights.claim: Chinese government agencies have reportedly discussed with Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu whether to keep allowing foreign users to download their AI model weights, alongside moves to limit overseas transfer of key training data.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A weights-export restriction would be self-defeating for Beijing's soft power and would hand distribution share back to US and European open-model releases.
insights.quote: Discussions have reportedly been held by Chinese government agencies with Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu on whether to allow their AI model weights to be downloaded by foreign users.
insights.locator: Discussions have reportedly been held

insights.claim: Restricting downloads of Chinese model weights would directly undercut the global popularity that Beijing's governance strategy depends on, putting China's security instincts in conflict with its diplomatic strategy.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Watch for any formal Chinese weights-export rule — it is the single policy that could stall the open-weight adoption trend.
insights.quote: Such restrictions would reduce the appeal of Chinese LLMs, potentially undercutting their global popularity.
insights.locator: Such restrictions would reduce the appeal

insights.claim: China has roughly 320 million gig-economy workers without labour-rights protection or social welfare provision, an unusually large and unprotected base of workers exposed to AI-driven displacement.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Domestic employment shock is the most plausible trigger for Beijing throttling AI deployment at home even while promoting it abroad.
insights.quote: With some 320 million people working in China’s ‘gig economy’ – without worker’s rights protection and social welfare provisions – the issue of under-employment is already a sensitive topic in China.
insights.locator: With some 320 million people working

insights.claim: The absence of comprehensive national policies to offset AI-induced job losses is identified as a blind spot for Beijing rather than a solved problem, despite China's otherwise detailed AI planning.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A labour-policy announcement from Beijing would signal that AI displacement has become politically live, and with it deployment restrictions.
insights.locator: Without comprehensive national policies to offset AI-induced job losses

themes.theme: The US pattern starting to break

insights.claim: Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 as an open-source, open-weight model, breaking the prevailing US closed-model pattern from one of the world's most valuable companies.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Nvidia benefits from open models proliferating regardless of which lab wins — its incentive is diffusion, not model exclusivity.
insights.quote: Nvidia, one of the world’s most valuable companies, has launched the open-source and open-weight Nemotron 3.5, breaking the US pattern.
insights.locator: Nvidia, one of the world’s most valuable companies

insights.claim: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has publicly called for lower US barriers to open-source AI specifically to compete with Chinese models, signalling that the US open-vs-closed settlement is contested.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: US policy drift toward open weights would erode the cost-and-customization edge that currently anchors Chinese AI diplomacy.
insights.quote: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has called for lower US barriers for open-source AI to compete with Chinese models.
insights.locator: But things could be changing

insights.claim: The US–China AI race is judged to be at an early stage with no determinable leader, because the two sides optimize for different objectives — diffusion and rule-setting versus proprietary capability and security.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Resist single-metric 'who's winning' narratives; position for both open-model diffusion and closed-frontier capability rather than one outcome.
insights.quote: In truth, the US–China AI race is still in its early stages. And so far, the two superpowers are competing on very different terms.
insights.locator: In truth, the US–China AI race
